name: Mang Den food guide
summary: Grilled chicken with lam rice is the plate Vietnam Tourism calls Mang Den’s signature. The tube is sticky rice and peanut salt. Pork skewers, porcupine, fried crickets, a tray of 40 or so indigenous vegetables, and wild banana-flower salad are the other dishes on Vietnam Tourism’s discover article. The weekend market names a longer list. A price is Check on arrival.
body: Eat the chicken as Vietnam Tourism describes it: free-range, fed on natural foods, grilled in the mountain style. Cơm lam comes out of a young bamboo tube with peanut salt, from a restaurant or a street vendor. The vendor’s street was not named. Thịt xiên is the skewer. Heo làng nướng, on the market list, is a separate name.

Porcupine and fried crickets are on the same Vietnam Tourism article. The porcupine is grilled, stuffed in bamboo shoots, cooked in soup, or packed in dong leaves. The crickets are the spiced snack with beer or Vietnamese wine. The vegetable tray is 40 or so indigenous vegetables, leaves, sprigs, and roots. The banana-flower salad uses a sweet-and-sour broth, chicken, pork or beef ears, herbs, and roasted peanuts. Vietnamese names for those four were not printed.

The weekend market is Chợ phiên Măng Đen, Saturday and Sunday. The Vietnam Tourism rural portal puts it on the pine hill along Hùng Vương in xã Măng Đen, Quảng Ngãi, with 24 stalls, and says it has run since October 2023. Báo Kon Tum puts it on the pine hill along Hùng Vương in thị trấn Măng Đen, opened 7 October 2023, with 24 stalls and then 32. Another Báo Kon Tum article puts it at Vườn thông by the district central square, from 7 October 2023, with more than 30 stalls at the start and more than 40 later. The opening hour is Check on arrival.
specialtiesLead: Vietnam Tourism names the chicken first. The weekend market and Báo Kon Tum name the rest. A price is Check on arrival.

sections.heading: The grill
paragraphs: The chicken, the bamboo-tube rice, and the pork skewer are the Vietnam Tourism plates. Cá nướng, cua nướng, and heo làng nướng are market names. An hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Grilled chicken
spots.note: Free-range chicken, grilled in the mountain style. Vietnam Tourism calls it the signature. The rural portal sells gà nướng cơm lam at the weekend market. A price is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Lam rice
spots.note: Sticky rice grilled in a young bamboo tube, with peanut salt. Restaurants and street vendors sell it. The street was not named. A price is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Grilled pork skewers
spots.note: Thick pieces of locally raised pork on a skewer. Báo Kon Tum names thịt xiên at the cultural night. A price is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Heo lang nuong
spots.note: A weekend-market specialty on the rural portal. A different name from the skewer and from smoked pork. A price is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Ca nuong
spots.note: On the rural portal’s specialty list. A species was not printed. A price is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Cua nuong
spots.note: On the same specialty list. A species was not printed. A price is Check on arrival.

sections.heading: Forest plate
paragraphs: Vietnam Tourism prints the porcupine, the crickets, the vegetable tray, and the banana-flower salad without Vietnamese names. The market list adds khổ qua rừng, cà đắng, măng rừng, and, on Báo Kon Tum, dried măng le.

spots.name: Porcupine
spots.note: A delicacy on Vietnam Tourism: grilled, stuffed in bamboo shoots, in soup, or packed in dong leaves. A Vietnamese name was not printed. A price is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Fried crickets
spots.note: A crunchy, spiced snack with beer or Vietnamese wine. Vietnam Tourism does not name a pub. A price is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Vegetable salad
spots.note: 40 or so indigenous vegetables, leaves, sprigs, and roots. A dressing was not printed. A price is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Forest banana salad
spots.note: Wild banana flowers, diced, with a sweet-and-sour broth, chicken, pork or beef ears, herbs, and roasted peanuts. A price is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Kho qua rung
spots.note: On the rural portal’s specialty list. A preparation was not printed. A price is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Ca dang
spots.note: On the same list. A preparation was not printed. A price is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Mang rung
spots.note: On the specialty list. Báo Kon Tum’s măng le is a separate dried-food name. A price is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Mang le
spots.note: Dried food on Báo Kon Tum, with trâu khô, bò khô, and thịt heo hun khói. A price is Check on arrival.

sections.heading: Dried and smoked
paragraphs: Three buffalo names, two beef names, and smoked pork. The articles do not say which names are one cut. A smoke time was not printed.

spots.name: Trau gac bep
spots.note: On the rural portal’s specialty list. Báo Kon Tum also names trâu khô and 3-star OCOP thịt trâu hun khói. A price is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Thit heo hun khoi
spots.note: Dried food on Báo Kon Tum, and a provincial 3-star OCOP product at the center stall. A visitor says thịt hun khói. A price is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Bo kho
spots.note: On the dried-food list. Thịt bò hun khói is the 3-star OCOP name at the center stall. The articles do not say these are one cut. A price is Check on arrival.

sections.heading: Cakes, nuts, and the jar
paragraphs: Bánh sừng trâu and hạt kơ nia are market foods. Bánh nếp is the cultural-night cake. Rượu cần is the jar. Cơm làng is the visitor’s name, not cơm lam.

spots.name: Banh sung trau
spots.note: On the specialty list. A visitor on Báo Kon Tum wrapped the cake at the market. A filling was not printed. A price is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Banh nep
spots.note: On the cultural-night meal with cơm lam, gà nướng, thịt xiên, and rượu cần. A filling was not printed. A price is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Hat de
spots.note: On the specialty list. A preparation was not printed. A price is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Hat ko nia
spots.note: Also written hạt cờ nia on the list. Almond-sized, thin brown shell, white kernel. The rural portal calls it béo ngậy, thơm, and ngọt bùi. A price is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Com lang
spots.note: A visitor on Báo Kon Tum names cơm làng at the market. A recipe was not printed. It is not cơm lam. A price is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Ruou can
spots.note: Fermented glutinous rice wine on the coolcation article, around a fire at night. The discover article describes homemade wine through a long bamboo straw. A strength and a price are Check on arrival.

sections.heading: Weekend market
paragraphs: Chợ phiên Măng Đen meets on Saturday and Sunday. The Vietnam Tourism rural portal puts the pine-hill grounds on Hùng Vương in xã Măng Đen, Quảng Ngãi, prints 24 stalls, and says the market has run since October 2023. Báo Kon Tum puts it on the pine hill along Hùng Vương in thị trấn Măng Đen, opened 7 October 2023, and prints 24 stalls, then 32. Another Báo Kon Tum article puts it at Vườn thông by the district central square and prints more than 30 stalls at the start and more than 40 later. The opening hour is Check on arrival.

The rural portal also names farm goods at the stalls: cà phê, mắc ca, gạo đỏ, organic vegetables, cherry tomatoes, pomelo, oranges, cucumber, and strawberries. A center stall sells wine products and specialty salt. Medicinal goods named there include hồng đẳng sâm, đương quy, sơn tra, chè dây, tinh bột nghệ, chuối hột, nấm linh chi cổ cò, sâm dây, giảo cổ lam, nấm lim xanh, and mật ong rừng. A price is Check on arrival.

sections.heading: Breakfast
paragraphs: Vietnam Tourism’s discover article puts a hot coffee at sunrise, while the town is in cloud. The coolcation article names locally grown Arabica with the lifting mist and does not say that cup is iced or hot. A cafe street was not named. The hour and the price are Check on arrival.

spots.name: Arabica coffee
spots.note: A hot cup at sunrise on the discover article. Locally grown Arabica on the coolcation article. The weekend market also sells cà phê as a farm good. A price is Check on arrival.
